Proposition
[Barrier derivative comparison] 1. ch14:14.3\group ch14-boundary-gradient Under the hypotheses of the preceding definition, $w^-\leq u\leq w^+$ throughout $\mathcal N\cap \Omega $. When the indicated normal derivatives exist, egin{equation} rac{\partial w^-}{\partial u }(x_0) \leq rac{\partial u}{\partial u }(x_0) \leq rac{\partial w^+}{\partial u }(x_0). ag {14.3} \end{equation} Uniformly bounded barrier gradients therefore give a boundary gradient bound.
Proof

\sketch Apply the comparison principle to $w^-$, $u$, and $w^+$ in $\mathcal N\cap \Omega $. Divide the resulting inequalities along the inward normal ray by the distance from $x_0$ and pass to the limit.

□

Two transformations will be used repeatedly. If $u=\psi (v)$ with $\psi \in C^2(I)$ and $\psi ' eq 0$, then egin{equation} Qu=\psi 'a^{ij}D_{ij}v+ rac{\psi ''}{(\psi ')^2}\mathcal E+b, ag {14.4} \end{equation} where the coefficient arguments are $(x,\psi (v),\psi 'Dv)$. If $u=v+\varphi $, then egin{equation} \widetilde Qv=Qu=a^{ij}D_{ij}v+a^{ij}D_{ij}\varphi +b. ag {14.5} \end{equation} Define egin{equation} \mathcal F(x,z,p,q)=a^{ij}(x,z,p)(p_i-q_i)(p_j-q_j). ag {14.6} \end{equation} For the transformed operator, egin{equation} \widetilde{\mathcal E}(x,v,Dv)=\mathcal F(x,u,Du,D\varphi ). ag {14.7} \end{equation}
